event.centerRule: God acts toward Israel in Egypt through Moses and Aaron while Pharaoh resists; departure, sea, first wilderness roads, and later memory remain visibly connected.

characterAnchors.label: God
characterAnchors.note: God hears Israel, commissions Moses, confronts Pharaoh, leads the departure, and is named throughout later memories of the Event.

characterAnchors.label: Moses
characterAnchors.note: Moses is called from Midian, speaks before Pharaoh and Israel, leads at the sea, and remains central in later retellings.

characterAnchors.label: Pharaoh
characterAnchors.note: Pharaoh orders labor, answers repeated demands and signs, releases Israel, and then pursues the departing people.

characterAnchors.label: Israel
characterAnchors.note: Israel grows under pressure, cries out, hears the signs, leaves Egypt, crosses the sea, sings, and enters the first wilderness roads.

characterAnchors.label: Aaron
characterAnchors.note: Aaron speaks and acts beside Moses before Israel and Pharaoh and remains present through the early journey.

characterAnchors.label: Miriam
characterAnchors.note: Miriam appears in the story of the child at the Nile and leads the women’s response after the sea crossing.

event.throughline: Israel grows under pressure in Egypt, cries out, and leaves through a long confrontation involving God, Moses, Aaron, and Pharaoh. The Event continues through the night of departure, the sea, song, and the first roads beyond, then remains active in later command, prayer, poetry, retelling, and reuse.

topic.orientation: The Exodus begins before the sea. Its trail moves from promise and arrival into oppression, call, confrontation, departure, crossing, song, and the first roads beyond. Later Scripture keeps returning to the Event in different forms without replacing the primary witness.
